title: Extended Product Warranties: To Buy or Not to Buy?
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss whether to buy extended product warranties, especially during the holiday shopping season. They argue that on average extended warranties are a losing bet (manufacturer warranties cover the first year, and only a small fraction of warranty money is paid out in repairs), note retailers like Circuit City and Best Buy earn significant profit from them, and describe situations where a warranty may make sense: high-dollar rear projection TVs (bulb life around 5,000 hours), laptops/PCs (repair likelihood), and cell phones for people prone to losing or breaking them. They cover reasons not to buy, including credit cards that automatically extend warranties, paying for a year already covered by the manufacturer, and shipping costs. Advice: research the product first, buy from the manufacturer rather than a big box retailer, and use the roughly thirty-day window to decide. The episode ends with a personal bad experience with a store-sold warranty on a washer and a listener email praising the show's fair treatment of prayer healing.

segments.title: Holiday season and the extended warranty question
segments.summary: Hosts open with holiday shopping banter and introduce the question of whether to buy an extended product warranty at the register.

segments.title: Averages, insurance and warranty profits
segments.summary: Hosts argue that on average an extended warranty is a losing bet, since manufacturer warranties cover the first year and few warranty dollars are paid out in repairs. They cite Circuit City and Best Buy relying on warranty revenue and a Business Week article about a cheap DVD player sold with a long warranty.

segments.title: When an extended warranty makes sense
segments.summary: Hosts describe cases where a warranty may be worth buying: high-dollar rear projection TVs whose bulbs are rated around 5,000 hours, PCs and laptops with a notable chance of repair within three years, and cell phones for people who lose or break phones, with the deductible considered.

segments.title: When not to buy and how to decide
segments.summary: Hosts explain reasons to skip the warranty: credit cards often extend manufacturer coverage automatically, the extended plan mostly adds two years after the first year of manufacturer coverage, and shipping costs can be high. Advice is to research products, buy from the manufacturer instead of a retailer, and use the roughly thirty-day window to decide.

segments.title: Personal washer and dryer warranty experience
segments.summary: Chuck describes a bad experience with a store-sold warranty on a washer and dryer, including seven service visits, wrong parts, and an unresponsive store that pointed to the repair contractor.

segments.title: Listener mail on prayer healing episode
segments.summary: Josh reads an email from listener Alexander praising the fair and balanced treatment of prayer and healing in an earlier episode.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts invite listener email and close the show.
